question: The correct relation between H (heat), I (current), R (resistance) and T (time) is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**H = I2 RT.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Point__**

 
• ​J [IMAGE: .......i] oule's Law states that when an electric current passes through a conductor, it produces heat due to the resistance of the conductor. The formula is: H = I² RT. where,

 
 
• H is the heat produced (in joules),

• R R" id="MathJax-Element-20-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">RR R" id="MathJax-Element-44-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">R R R R R RR is the resistance (in ohms),
 
• T T" id="MathJax-Element-21-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">TT T" id="MathJax-Element-45-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">T T T T T TT is the time (in seconds) for which the current flows.
 
 
 
• Joule's Law helps us understand the relationship between electricity and heat generation, allowing for safer and more efficient electrical designs.
 
• It has various applications such as: 
 
 
• **Electric Heaters:** The Joule's Law can applied in electric heating devices, where resistive heating is used to generate warmth.
 
• **Fuses:** The heat generated by the excess current discontinue the circuit.
 
• **Wiring:** In electrical installations, the resistance of wires must be considered to prevent excessive heat buildup, which can lead to fires.
